evals.prompt: Our /api/invoices/:id/pdf endpoint returns a PDF with the wrong currency symbol for customers in Switzerland (shows € instead of CHF). It started after we upgraded the i18n library last week. Debug this.
evals.expected_output: Builds a tight red-capable feedback loop first (failing test or curl asserting the CHF symbol), reproduces and minimises, then generates ranked falsifiable hypotheses before instrumenting.
expectations: Proposes building a feedback loop (e.g. a failing test or curl script) that asserts the exact symptom (CHF vs €) before reading code to form a theory
Considers a differential or bisection loop across the i18n library upgrade (old vs new version, or git bisect run)
Plans to minimise the repro until every remaining element is load-bearing
Plans 3-5 ranked hypotheses each with a falsifiable prediction, shown to the user before testing
Plans to tag temporary debug logs with a unique prefix (e.g. [DEBUG-xxxx]) and grep them out at cleanup

evals.prompt: The test `OrderQueue processes jobs in priority order` fails maybe once every 30 CI runs, never locally. Can you diagnose it?
evals.expected_output: Treats it as non-deterministic: aims to raise the reproduction rate (loop 100x, parallelise, stress, inject sleeps) to get a debuggable loop before hypothesising.
expectations: Frames the goal as raising the reproduction rate rather than getting a clean single repro
Proposes running the test in a loop (e.g. 100x), in parallel, or under stress / injected sleeps to narrow timing windows
Refuses to hypothesise about the cause until a red-capable loop with a pinned reproduction rate exists
Proposes making the loop deterministic where possible (seeding RNG, pinning time, isolating state)

evals.prompt: Search on our product catalog page went from ~200ms to ~3s after the last sprint. Figure out why and fix it.
evals.expected_output: Follows the perf branch: establish a baseline measurement and bisect rather than add logs, then fix with a regression check and a post-mortem.
expectations: Establishes a baseline timing measurement (timing harness, profiler or query plan) as the feedback loop before guessing
Proposes bisecting across the sprint's changes (e.g. git bisect run with the timing harness)
Says logs are usually the wrong tool for performance regressions — measure first, fix second
Plans to add a regression test before the fix only if a correct seam exists, and to note the absence of a seam as a finding otherwise
Ends with a post-mortem asking what would have prevented it, handing off to /improve-codebase-architecture if architectural
